rename.from: @EnableRuleMigrationSupport causes Exceptions to be silently ignored
rename.to: ExpectedExceptionSupport causes exceptions to be silently ignored

body:
**Analysis**

(_sharing the results of my brainstorming session here_)

The cause of the bug is that `AbstractTestRuleSupport.handleTestExecutionException(ExtensionContext, Throwable)` effectively swallows the exception if there are no registered instances of the `ExpectedException` rule.

My first attempt to fix the bug was to count the number of _members_ that were discovered by having `invokeAppropriateMethodOnRuleAnnotatedMembers()` return the number of members. I then rethrew the exception if the number of members was zero. However, this did not fix the bug since `ExpectedExceptionSupport.handleTestExecutionException(ExtensionContext, Throwable)` invokes `AbstractTestRuleSupport.handleTestExecutionException()` twice: once for fields and once for methods. Since the "member count" does not aggregate across fields + methods, the counting logic is fundamentally broken.

But... to _fix_ the bug, we will in fact have to count the number of _members_ registered; otherwise, we don't know if the adapter is supposed to rethrow the exception.

FYI: I have pushed my _work in progress_ to the following branch in case anyone wants to pick this up.

https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/tree/issues/1069-expected-exception-support-bug

I'm unassigning myself for the time being.

The good news is that this is not a show stopper 🐛.

There are two simple **workarounds**! 😉 

1. If you annotate your test class with `@EnableRuleMigrationSupport`, you then must declare an `ExpectedException` rule even if you don't _use_ it per se -- for example, `@Rule public ExpectedException thrown = ExpectedException.none();`.
2. If you don't want to declare an `ExpectedException` rule that you don't use, then you cannot use `@EnableRuleMigrationSupport`. Instead, you can register only the migration support extensions that you actually need -- for example, `@ExtendWith({ExternalResourceSupport.class, VerifierSupport.class})`.
@algielen, please let us know if the above workarounds work for you.
@sbrannen I only need ExternalResourceSupport.class for now. I tested the workaround 2 and it works indeed :)
